text:
Ryan Shea took a long road to an NHL top four: a fourth-round pick in 2015, years in the minors, then Pittsburgh, and now 23 minutes a night in Edmonton. Saturday brought the unlucky kind of headline, when his attempted shoot-in struck teammate Ryan Nugent-Hopkins in the side of the head. Nobody wants to be part of that play.

On the ice, he has been useful in a quiet way. Edmonton takes about 52% of the expected goals with him on, nearly five points better than without him, though the scoring hasn't followed: five points in 18 games and two in his last ten. Oilersnation has argued for splitting him from Connor Murphy, which tells you the pairing is being watched.

The fascinating number is from last season. Evolving-Hockey had him worth 3.3 wins, fifth among all defensemen, but with the caveat that his results ran well ahead of his chances (1.9 expected wins). That's a big season he's unlikely to repeat, and this year looks like the more honest version. He also draws more penalties than he takes. Our range projects 27 to 46 points over a full season, which feels high for how he's actually used.
headline: Shea's long road to big minutes
